title: Copilot Studio: Dataverse tables as a native knowledge source for agents
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, Dataverse prerequisites, control paths, inspection API and billing qualifications are supported. One minor clarification should specify that a fresh index and full synchronization follow re-enablement after search has been off for 12 hours.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans native Dataverse knowledge grounding in structured enterprise records, customer data, operational data and business application content.
claims.quote: We are enabling Microsoft Dataverse as a native knowledge source in Copilot Studio, expanding the platform’s ability to ground AI agents in structured enterprise data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dataverse search respects Dataverse security roles and permissions.

claims.quote: Generative mode: UnlimitedClassic mode: Two Dataverse knowledge sources (and up to 15 tables per knowledge source) | Agent user's Microsoft Entra ID authentication

claims.claim: An agent surfaces only content that the asking user can access when using authenticated knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Agent user authentication for knowledge sources means that when a specific user asks a question of the agent, the agent only surfaces content that the specific user can access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes its index within 12 hours.
claims.quote: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes the index within 12 hours.

claims.quote: Sources of these types that you added before the setting changed stay configured on the agent, but the agent might not be able to retrieve from them.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Studio measures and meters agent usage in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The standard-harness generative-answer feature rate is 2 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Generative answer | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge

claims.claim: The billing example totals 12 credits from 10 tenant-graph-grounding credits and 2 generative-answer credits.
claims.quote: An agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 Copilot Credits (10 Copilot Credits for tenant graph grounding, and 2 Copilot Credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter and Indirect cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate Dataverse-knowledge-specific rate or price was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "knowledge" "Copilot" "price" "rate". Read requirements-messages-management, billing-credit-overview, both Dataverse knowledge articles and search configuration; general feature and capacity charges are documented, not a separate Dataverse-knowledge price.

claims.claim: Dataverse is a supported generative-answers knowledge source for standard-harness agents.
claims.quote: Dataverse knowledge sources | 2 sources with up to 15 tables each

claims.claim: Applicable additional feature or reasoning-model charges can accompany a generative answer.
claims.quote: Each interaction with an agent might use multiple feature types at the same time.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness agents use a different usage-based billing structure.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Eligible standard-harness employee-facing usage is included in Microsoft Copilot USL when operating as the authenticated licensed user.
claims.quote: are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user of the agent is licensed with Microsoft Copilot, and the agent operates using the authenticated Microsoft Copilot USL user's identity.

claims.claim: That inclusion is subject to fair usage limits.
claims.quote: Usage is limited to fair usage limits. Microsoft reserves the right to update the limits as the product evolves, and new usage patterns emerge.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness agent usage is not included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Usage by agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness isn't included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Mixed licensing reflects metered usage and eligible usage included in a licensed user's subscription.
claims.quote: Generative answer | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge

claims.where: controls[1]; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can set a monthly consumption limit for each Copilot Studio agent, not for individual tables.
claims.quote: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for each Copilot Studio agent, regardless of whether the environment uses prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Per-agent monthly limits apply with either prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for each Copilot Studio agent, regardless of whether the environment uses prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure notifications as the agent approaches its limit.
claims.quote: Notifications: Admins, both at the environment and tenant level, receive alerts when an agent's usage approaches the defined limit.

claims.claim: A configurable hard stop automatically turns off the agent when it hits its limit.
claims.quote: After you set limits, you can configure two key guardrails: Notifications ... Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.

claims.claim: The agent's monthly limit does not stop agent flows it calls.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls.

claims.claim: Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately.
claims.quote: Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately, and new agent flow runs are blocked only when the environment has no Copilot Credits available.

claims.claim: Agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Indirect cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The multiline-text and file preview section warns of extra Dataverse capacity costs for creating a search index.
claims.quote: Creating a search index incurs extra Dataverse capacity costs.

claims.claim: The general platform rule counts Dataverse search against tenant storage entitlements, independently of the column preview.
claims.quote: Dataverse search counts towards the different storage entitlements you have in the tenant.

claims.claim: Dataverse search is part of database storage consumption.
claims.quote: Dataverse search is part of database storage consumption in the Summary and Dataverse tabs.

claims.claim: Administrators can inspect indexed tables and their individual capacity consumption.
claims.quote: To export usage granular reports and view exactly which tables are being indexed and how much capacity each one consumes, see view dataverse search storage.

claims.claim: Only virtual tables using the Finance and Operations data provider are selectable.
claims.quote: Virtual tables | Only virtual tables that use the Finance and Operations data provider can be selected.
